market_definition.boundary_notes: The available sizing treats freight brokerage and load-matching software as one object [S1]. A boundary that matters and is not addressed: freight brokerage software is not the same as the freight brokerage market itself, and the two differ by orders of magnitude. Within the software boundary, the load board is the established form factor — a marketplace holding carrier relationships — rather than a point tool [S2].

saturation.consolidation_activity: None seen. No source here reports an acquisition in this category.
saturation.why: Two named incumbents, and a category explicitly described as fragmented with many regional players [S1] — which means the competitor count found here (2) badly understates the real number and should not be read as a thin field. Fragmentation is the strongest signal available and it points both ways: there is room, and there is a crowd. The specific constraint is not saturation but distribution: the incumbents hold most carrier relationships and have already shipped matching automation [S2], so a new entrant needs a reason for carriers to add a second tool. Pricing direction, new-entrant flow and consolidation are all unknown, so this read rests on two facts rather than five.

absorption_risk.notes: 'Contested' rather than 'feature' is the right reading and the distinction is load-bearing. The incumbents have shipped the capability [S2], which is what absorption looks like starting — but the category remains fragmented with many regional players [S1], which is the opposite of what a fully absorbed category looks like. Both facts are in the evidence and they pull in different directions. The honest position is that absorption is underway at the national level while regional room persists, and that a new entrant's survival depends on the regional half being real. No precedents are cited because nothing in this material documents a comparable case.
